That matters for Bryce Young because center stability and run-game fit can affect protection and offensive consistency. [5]
- **Bryce Young (QB) / Tetairoa McMillan (WR)** — Young and McMillan posted an 81.3 passer rating on their targets last season, fifth-worst among WR-QB pairs with at least 75 targets. The connection was usable, but the stat points to room for growth in McMillan’s WR1 ceiling and Young’s passing efficiency. [3]
- **Bryce Young (QB)** — Young enters 2026 on a contract-year “prove it” season, with Carolina still deciding whether he’s worth a long-term top-of-market extension. For fantasy, that keeps his outlook tied to actual progression rather than assumed stability. [1]
- **Ejiro Evero (DC)** — Carolina is still dealing with a defense that ranked dead last in quarterback pressure rate at 26.2%, and Evero’s unit has produced the fewest quarterback traps in the league over his 51-game span. It’s mostly a defense note, but it helps explain why the Panthers keep emphasizing the trenches. [2]

HOU.summary:
- **Justin Watson (WR)** — He was getting first-team reps with the Texans’ offense during minicamp and was singled out as a surprising player who could make the roster. That puts him squarely in the WR depth battle and makes him the clearest non-starter to monitor for a possible Week 1 role. [2]

- **Tank Dell (WR)** — Dell is trending in the right direction, working off to the side in wide receiver drills and running, but he is not yet a full participant. For fantasy, that keeps his route volume and target-share outlook in wait-and-see mode until training camp clarifies how close he is to a full return. [3]

- **Trent Brown (OT)** — Houston used multiple offensive line combinations in minicamp, and Brown kept popping up with the first team while the staff sorts out its starting five. That doesn’t change a fantasy lineup directly, but it matters for pass protection and the run game as the Texans build their offensive environment. [1]

JAX.summary:
- **Chris Rodriguez Jr. (RB)** — He’s projected to play an important early role in Liam Coen’s offense and to handle a healthy dose of carries after Travis Etienne Jr.’s departure. Jacksonville wants more physicality in the run game, and Rodriguez’s interior-running profile gives him real early-down fantasy appeal. [2]

- **Boerkircher (TE)** — He looks set to be the clear No. 2 tight end on the depth chart, with the staff valuing his run- and pass-blocking versatility and seeing untapped potential as a receiver. That matters because it puts him on the field more and gives him a path to a secondary TE role, even if the volume ceiling is modest. [1]

- **Brian Picucci (running game coordinator)** — Liam Coen’s new running game coordinator is the lone notable addition to the offensive coaching staff, and his long history with Coen suggests continuity in how Jacksonville wants to build the ground attack. That supports the idea of a more intentional run-game emphasis, which could reinforce RB usage patterns. [3]

LAC.summary:
- **Quentin Johnston (WR)** — OTAs/minicamp have treated Johnston like a core piece of the passing game, and the lack of a major outside WR addition reads as a quiet endorsement of his spot alongside Ladd McConkey and Tre Harris. That keeps Johnston in the mix for meaningful weekly volume if the staff continues to feature him. [4]

- **Mike McDaniel (OC)** — McDaniel is steering the Chargers toward wide-zone run concepts and is changing Justin Herbert’s footwork to get the ball out faster, with the stated goal of creating more YAC and more explosive plays. For fantasy, that points to a more efficient passing environment for the skill players, even though specific target/carry shares are not specified. [1]

TB.summary: - **Chris Godwin (WR)** — Zac Robinson used Godwin in the slot for most of OTAs, and he reportedly caught plenty of passes with a few TDs in 7-on-7 work. That points to a high-volume, PPR-friendly role inside as Tampa Bay searches for its WR1; the exact target hierarchy is not specified, but Godwin’s usage looked encouraging. [1]

TEN.summary:
- **Carnell Tate (WR)** — He was one of the standouts of OTAs, flashing speed, crisp routes and multiple one-handed grabs. Tennessee and Cam Ward are clearly looking for an elite target, so Tate’s early showing matters as a rookie who could push into the passing-game mix if it carries into minicamp. [1]

- **Titans WR battle** — Tyren Montgomery, Xavier Restrepo and K.J. Osborn are competing for what looks like one or two roster spots, and the article says their OTAs were excellent. That keeps the back end of Tennessee’s receiver depth chart volatile and gives mandatory minicamp real fantasy relevance for the WR3/WR4 picture. [2]
